blurb: Beyond batteries — pumped hydro, compressed air, thermal, hydrogen, gravity, and long-duration storage, mapped on the duration-versus-cost axis.
question: How should this energy be stored?
title: Energy Storage: A Practical Reference
lede: Storage is bought by the hour: the technologies that win at minutes lose badly at weeks, and the killer axis is discharge duration versus cost per stored kWh. This guide catalogs {{N_ENTRIES}} technologies across seven classes, from pumped hydro to green hydrogen and virtual storage.

facets.label: Role
facets.tip: Grid or energy-system services the technology mainly sells. Most projects stack several.

facets.label: Duration
facets.tip: Economic discharge duration at rated power: Minutes <1 h · Hours 1–10 h · Days 10–100 h · Weeks+ 100 h and beyond. Most technologies span a band; tanks and caverns stretch it.

facets.label: Efficiency
facets.tip: Directional round-trip efficiency, electricity in to electricity out. For heat-output technologies the tag reflects power-to-heat delivery instead — see each entry. Untagged where round-trip framing doesn't apply.

facets.label: Cost
facets.tip: Directional installed cost per kWh of energy capacity (the number that matters for long duration — power-conversion $/kW is separate and covered in each entry). Thermal entries that sell heat are costed per thermal kWh.

facets.label: Maturity
facets.tip: Deployed at scale = GW-class installed base · Commercial = bankable projects at smaller scale · Pilot = demonstration or first-of-a-kind commercial · R&D = lab and startup stage.
